newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sandoz nutrition sees faster growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Sandoz nutrition sees faster growth in 97.

text.p: Sales at Sandoz AG's Nutrition Division have been less than satisfactory so far this year but growth has accelerated since the summer and the division should show an increasing trend in 1997, David Pyott, head of Sandoz Nutrition said.

Sales have grown by between two and three percent in local currencies in the year-to-date, but the division is targeting year-on-year growth of between four and six percent for 1997, Pyott said during a conference call with analysts.
"We are focusing on high growth, high value added material. The vast majority of our products are health oriented and we're going to offer above industry average volume growth," he said.
Nutrition accounts for some 15 percent of sales at Sandoz. The division had sales of 2.7 billion Swiss francs for the first nine months of 1996.

"This year to date we haven't done as well as I had hoped, we have just between two and three percent growth in local currencies of which volume is about one-and-a-half percent and price is one percent," Pyott also said.
He said the focus of future efforts in clinical nutrition will be to try and build the segment's global position. He said the company is currently number two worldwide.
In health foods, Pyott said Sandoz was concentrating all its growth efforts Europe.
The strategic thrust in infant and baby foods will be to build up the company's position in Western Europe.
He is also looking to further food drink volume growth in Southeast Asia while maintaining volumes in Europe at good profitability levels.
In addition, he said the Center of Science for Public Interest in the U.S. had been critical of the company's use of sugar and modified food starch in some of its products.
In response to this problem, Sandoz Nutrition will have reformulated more than 128 products by the end of this quarter, Pyott said.
This reformulation is costing the company leas than $10 million per annum and these costs should not result in a decline in margins, he added. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
